themes.name: Assessment of Professional Competencies
themes.definition: The development, validation, and adaptation of instruments to measure professional competencies in engineering students, including technical, interpersonal, and ethical skills. Focuses on identifying and validating constructs such as employability, self-efficacy, and professional responsibility.
evidence: [LHGYXXJG] The study aims to identify indicators that can measure students' employability skills and attributes. The research model, based on The Conference Board of Canada (Employability Skills 2000+), is divided into fundamental skills, personal management skills, and cooperative skills.

[IV425BDL] Consequently, new competencies have been incorporated into engineering curricula, with ethics education emphasizing social responsibility as a core competency for students. This paper aims to adapt the 'Engineering Professional Responsibility Assessment (EPRA)' to Turkish culture.

[KI4LCCHP] This study aimed to validate the factor structure of professional competencies in engineering and test the measurement invariance of these competencies across gender. Through a cross-sectional survey, 552 senior undergraduate students responded to a 24-item professional competencies scale.

themes.name: Self-Efficacy Measurement in Engineering
themes.definition: The development and validation of scales to assess students' self-efficacy in engineering-related tasks, including programming, design, and general engineering skills. Focuses on the reliability and validity of these instruments across different contexts and demographics.
evidence: [2DDA52FC] Two scales for engineering self-efficacy have recently been developed for undergraduate students, with validity evidence relating self-efficacy responses to persistence and achievement in engineering.

[CJPX792Z] Contribution: This article has shown that self-efficacy in performing complex computer programming tasks and the self-regulation of electrical and electronics engineering undergraduate students varies with respect to the class standing and prior experience in computer programming.
[U374P6MT] The purpose of this study is to adapt a well-known self-efficacy scale and determine engineering student's C++ computer programming self-efficacy levels.

themes.name: Motivation and Learning Strategies Assessment
themes.definition: The validation and adaptation of instruments to measure students' motivational attitudes, learning strategies, and engagement in engineering education. Includes the use of Likert scales and factor analysis to assess constructs such as intrinsic and extrinsic motivation.
evidence: [CY59SPDS] This research paper reports the quantitative validation of instruments for assessing engineering students' motivational attitudes and behaviors in their capstone design course. Motivation plays a key role in engineering practice, particularly with respect to students' efficiency and effectiveness as well as their readiness to engage in teamwork.
[PYM3MQNK] The aims of this work were to investigate the dimensionality of the motivated strategies for learning questionnaire (MSLQ) and compare the validation of the three competing models.

[NLXE3X6S] Using the definition of sustainability from the Brundtland report and expectancy value theory, students’ sentiment toward SE was evaluated using items to assess SE self-efficacy, SE value and SE affect.

themes.name: Entrepreneurial Mindset and Design Skills
themes.definition: The development and validation of instruments to measure entrepreneurial mindset constructs, such as 'Connections' and 'Creating Value,' as well as design mindset and creativity in engineering students. Focuses on the use of factor analysis and confirmatory models.
evidence: [K9E5C83P] This Work in Progress paper will describe the initial steps of validating an instrument to measure Connections and Creating Value skills in undergraduate engineering students. Cultivating an entrepreneurial mindset and associated behaviors in first-year engineering students is one step towards fostering students' professional skill development.

[6XVSWITA] This article defines and operationalizes the construct design mindset and introduces the Design Mindset Inventory (D-Mindset0.1), allowing us to measure and leverage statistical analyses to advance our understanding of its role in design.

[YE4TP358] Creativity, being a key competency of engineering, must be taught and assessed. Here, we verify the reliability of the Creative Engineering Design Assessment (CEDA), a psychometric test for engineering students, as well as clarify the assessment process.

themes.name: Internship and Workplace Experience Evaluation
themes.definition: The adaptation and validation of instruments to assess students' perceptions of their internship and workplace experiences, including competencies developed and satisfaction with the learning environment. Focuses on the use of confirmatory factor analysis and reliability testing.
evidence: [DFVK7NR2] The purpose of this study was to validate a newly adapted version of the Work Experience Questionnaire (WEQ), which can be used for evaluating engineering students' perception of their internship experience.

[XHXW8PNL] The purpose of this paper is to assess engineering students’ perceptions of their internship experiences. For that purpose, the validation of a recently adapted version of the Work Experience Questionnaire (WEQ) was carried out on a sample of 447 engineering students.

[9CXV3IJ6] The apprenticeship course is suitable for trail and test under the supervision of academic educators and industry experts. The essential part of the practical skills training occurs during this period. In general, the apprenticeship course leads to acquiring valuable practical experiences and improving behavior and attitudes of students.

themes.name: Systems Thinking and Problem-Solving Skills
themes.definition: The assessment of systems thinking skills (STS) and problem-solving competencies in engineering students, including the use of surveys and diagnostic activities to measure these skills. Focuses on the development of instruments and cross-comparisons for validation.
evidence: [J8H6TD8Q] It is widely acknowledged that systems thinking skills (STS) are critical competencies that enable engineering students to solve problems, communicate, use data, and design components and systems, with greater success.
[IQD3WXLQ] Industry-Coupled Problem-Based Learning (IC-PBL) has become a central approach in engineering education, enabling students to bridge theoretical understanding with real-world application.

themes.name: Communication Skills Assessment
themes.definition: The development and validation of instruments to measure workplace oral communication skills and other communication-related competencies in engineering students. Focuses on the use of factor analysis and reliability testing to ensure validity.
evidence: [4I9HTBU4] One of the most crucial factors that influence the success of a construction project is communication. However, past studies found that communication failure frequently occurs at civil engineering workplaces. Among communication failures reported were oral communications, such as giving instruction and briefing; skills, which are supposed to be mastered by engineering graduates during their study years.

[XT6BBTKW] As there is currently no comprehensive measure that allows researchers, program evaluators, and outreach advisors to examine ambassadors' professional development and growth, this study sought to develop and validate an Ambassador Questionnaire (AQ).

themes.name: Mathematical and Technical Competence Measurement
themes.definition: The development and validation of instruments to assess mathematical and technical competencies in engineering students, including the use of Rasch analysis and think-aloud protocols to determine item difficulty and student ability.
evidence: [HX8CUXK4] This article reports about our efforts to determine engineering students' competence in mathematics. Our research is embedded in a larger project, KoM@ING–Modeling and developing competence: Integrated IRT based and qualitative studies with a focus on mathematics and its usage in engineering studies.

[VG98XEQP] In this research study, we are interested in assessing students' perceptions of working on a community-partnered project in their first year of engineering. The Likert scale questions included questions on engineering, design, and tinkering self-efficacy, intentions to persist, and sense of belonging scale.

data.meta_observations: The abstracts predominantly focus on the development, validation, and adaptation of assessment instruments for engineering students. The most frequently observed themes include professional competencies, self-efficacy, and motivation. There is a notable emphasis on the use of factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, and reliability testing to validate these instruments. Some abstracts lack detailed methodological descriptions or results, which limits the depth of analysis for certain themes.
data.grounding_notes: All themes and evidence are grounded in verbatim quotes from the abstracts. No external frameworks or categories were imposed. The frequency of themes is based on the number of abstracts explicitly addressing each theme. Some themes, such as 'Communication Skills Assessment' and 'Mathematical and Technical Competence Measurement,' are less frequently observed in this batch.
